summary.headline: Shriram Properties FY26 revenue rose 39% to INR1,357 crores and net profit crossed INR100 crores for the first time, with FY27 guidance of INR3,300-3,500 crores sales value.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,357 crores (+39% YoY) and net profit rose 30% to INR101 crores, driven by a strong Q4 handover push in Bangalore, Chennai and Kolkata. Full-year sales value was flat at INR2,354 crores, with Q4 sales of INR663 crores, as several launches slipped due to approval delays, mainly in Bangalore. Management guided FY27 to be stronger than FY26, with sales value of INR3,300-3,500 crores, collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units. Analysts pressed on margins, the rising other-expense line, the cash flow trend, and the funding of new land acquisitions; management said these would be funded from completed-project cash flows and possibly intermittent debt.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Core market; Songs of the Earth launch sold over 85% in launch year. Management says the growth strategy is centred on Bangalore and Pune, with North Bangalore flagged for higher pricing upside.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Maiden launch at Undri (Spectrum) sold over 300 units in under a year, against roughly 850 units absorbed annually by the micro-market over the last three years. Pune revenue is recognised under percentage-of-completion.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Land settlement with the Government of West Bengal done; 314 acres originally, 42 acres surrendered, 100+ acres still available. Skyblooms Villas over 50% sold and Signature Square about 40% sold at launch. Approval exists for 2.3 million sq ft of apartments, with plotted development planned.

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Contributed to Q4 revenue recognition from completed projects; a launch is expected within about a week of the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume guidance of 5-5.5 million sq ft and sales value of INR3,300-3,500 crores.
FY27 collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units.
FY27 pipeline addition of 7-8 million sq ft and GDV addition of INR5,000-6,000 crores; land-related capital commitment of INR350-400 crores.
FY27 project completions of about 3.8 million sq ft, with revenue recognition potential of about INR1,740 crores.
Mission FY28 targets: sales of INR5,000 crores, revenue of INR2,500 crores and PBT of INR250 crores; management reiterated PBT margin of 10-11%.
Management expects 8-9% PAT margin on a normalised 3-year basis, with the effective tax rate below 25% due to carried-forward losses.
Construction capital spend of INR900-1,000 crores expected in FY27, versus roughly INR90-95 crores per quarter recently.
Finance costs may decline slightly, but gross debt of about INR600 crores will continue; the company may take intermittent bridge debt.
capex_capacity: Ongoing projects: 16.7 million sq ft, 85% sold; 2.6 million sq ft unsold in ongoing projects, plus 18.6 million sq ft upcoming pipeline; total unsold potential over 21 million sq ft, GDV about INR13,950 crores.
Seven projects acquired during FY26; approvals under way; over 7 million sq ft expected to enter the launch pipeline in the next 3-6 months. Target to double the upcoming pipeline in 18-24 months.
FY26 completed and delivered 8 projects, about 4 million sq ft. FY27 target of about 6 million sq ft launches across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata.

New business development investment of INR372 crores in FY26, one of the highest annual outlays; about 80% of cumulative operating cash of over INR900 crores over four years was reinvested into new projects.
Liquidity of over INR520 crores: cash of INR172 crores plus undrawn funding lines of INR358 crores. Equity about INR1,460 crores; cost of debt 11.2%; CRISIL A-/Positive.
demand_pricing: FY26 sales value INR2,354 crores (marginal increase); sales volume 4.15 million sq ft; Q4 sales INR663 crores. Management said a couple of Q4 launches slipped into Q1 FY27.

Pricing: management expects organic price growth of no more than 5-6% a year, against 8-10% construction cost inflation; margin protection rather than expansion is the aim. Tiles, paints and PVC windows face 5-10% price pressure.
Management flagged IT employment trends, interest rate affordability and longer sales cycles as sector risks; focus is on mid and upper-mid housing.
Kolkata: management said the new state government is positive. Long-term outlook strong, but near-term recovery expected to be slower than Bangalore or Pune.
Competition: management said the market favours branded and organised developers.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising operating cash outflows and higher new-project investment lead to a cash crunch or more debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 free cash flow fell slightly due to construction spend ahead of finishing stages; no additional debt is needed for construction, as liquidity is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR126 crores to INR172 crores, and will they rise further in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said higher accelerated revenue recognition (about INR1,200 crores vs about INR800 crores) brought about INR25 crores of brokerage charges, with INR7 crores impairment on Bengal land and INR10 crores of provisions; he said other expenses should not rise in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What PBT and PAT margins should be assumed?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said PBT margin of 10-11% is the target; PAT margin is expected to be 8-9% on a normalised 3-year basis, because the effective tax rate may be below 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 presales slightly below the INR2,600 crore guidance, and why are there few Kolkata launches?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said a couple of projects slipped into Q1 FY27, with one launched that week and another in Chennai in about a week. Kolkata plotted development is being tested before the remaining 100+ acres are monetised; 2.3 million sq ft of apartment approval is already in hand.

qa_highlights.question: When will construction spend ramp up, and how much new project investment is planned in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said construction capital spend is expected at INR900-1,000 crores in FY27. The 8 million sq ft pipeline addition implies INR350-400 crores of land commitment, to be funded from completed-project cash flows and possibly bridge debt.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,000 crore revenue recognition potential over three years conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said ongoing projects alone can deliver about INR4,400 crores, to be unlocked in 2-3 years. Upside exists from Kolkata and the pipeline, but management preferred conservative guidance.

risks_watch: Approval delays (approvals, e-Khata, OCs, Kaveri portal) that caused FY26 launch slippage and could affect FY27 launches of about 6 million sq ft.
Other expenses (INR172 crores) and provisions, including the INR10 crore recoverable from a landowner; management said these should not rise in FY27.
Operating cash flow fell YoY, and construction capex is set to rise to INR900-1,000 crores in FY27; monitor collections against the INR2,100-2,200 crore guidance.
Rising material costs (tiles, paints, PVC) and limited ability to pass on price increases beyond 5-6%.
Finance costs and net debt; management said gross debt of about INR600 crores will stay and bridge debt may be taken.
Q1 FY27 launch execution: Chennai project and Kolkata plotted development.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 recovery and FY27 visibility, but deliberately conservative on guidance because of geopolitical, consumer confidence and IT employment uncertainty. Management said upside exists if conditions improve, and it declined to commit to exact numbers beyond the stated FY27 KPI ranges.
key_quotes: Therefore, while we remain cautious in the near term in terms of our guidance to the market on FY '27 KPIs, we are fully geared to seize the opportunities in the market and sustain our growth momentum in FY '27 and beyond.

Margin protection is real. Margin enhancement happens only through new project -- new micro portfolio upgrades where you enter better micro markets or launch projects in new micro market, which have a higher pricing potential.
But for now, I think it will be better to be conservative than saying something which is very big and then pulling back.
